docs.purpose: Powers the admin App Health Dashboard: pulls together five live health signals about the mobile app (crash rate, sign-in success rate, how often people save a lead after viewing one, how often they convert on the paywall, and cache-refresh activity) so the team can see at a glance whether the app is working properly for users.
docs.data_story: It touches no table at all. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 6 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-app-health/api/useAppHealth.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

versioning.why: Every consumer is in src/** and ships in the same Next.js deploy as the route, so a breaking change is one commit.

inputs.why: ESCALATION (Spec 128 §4): it reads no table and no contract — every value comes from the Sentry REST API and the PostHog query API. The closed menu (contract · app_outputs · device · props · none) has no member for "an external SaaS API", and "none" would be false.

outputs.why: A QUERY contract writes nothing; the handler issues no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE anywhere in the file or in the libs it calls.
evidence: src/app/api/admin/app-health/route.ts — read in full 2026-09-15; no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE reached

state.why: A CONTRACT holds no client state: every value is resolved per request on the server and nothing is cached in a client store by the route itself.

staleness.why: ESCALATION (Spec 128 §4): served from a 60s in-process minute-boundary memo of two external SaaS APIs. The menu has live · query_cache (TanStack) · snapshot (a pipeline-written projection) · static · none, and none of them describes an in-process TTL over a third-party API.

evidence: src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:150-201 — classifyRoute executed 2026-09-15 with the concrete path

rls_class.why: It reaches no table, so no RLS class applies.

checks.why: guards.session must equal classifyRoute("/api/admin/app-health"), executed 2026-09-15 → "admin" plus the in-handler guard (verifyAdminAuth at src/app/api/admin/app-health/route.ts:85). Locked by admin-app-health-route-exports.logic.test.ts, admin-app-health.infra.test.ts.
Every declared error class returns the { data, error, meta } envelope of docs/specs/00_engineering_standards.md §4.4; expected to stay at zero deviations.

The response is an explicit pick-by-name of 6 field(s) (src/app/api/admin/app-health/route.ts:178-193), so a column added upstream cannot leak; this check set-equals the projection to inputs.field_whitelist.

errors.why: Success and failure both arrive in the { data, error, meta } envelope of docs/specs/00_engineering_standards.md §4.4; withApiEnvelope is the outermost wrapper and converts any uncaught throw into the same shape.

emits.why: It emits named observability events only — Sentry breadcrumbs and/or PostHog captures; it writes no ledger row.

limitations.what: a11y.touch_target_min_px has no legal answer for a CONTRACT
limitations.measured: The schema allows only UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44; a JSON endpoint has no touch target and the vocabulary has no "n/a". Left UNRESEARCHED and escalated per Spec 128 §4 rather than invented.
